Hi, I am a linux newbie who recently switched from windows to ubuntu. When I installed it, I was unable to make a large partition for ubuntu, and I am now running low on space. I am thinking about reinstalling ubuntu to my entire hard drive, but I am unsure about how to backup my files. Is there a linux program that I could use to clone my hard drive before reinstalling?

-Sorry about my lack of technical vocabulary, this is still all pretty new to me.
Best way to increase partition size?

You can install gparted on a Live CD/USB with sudo apt-get install gparted . Load up the Live environment and then install and run gparted and it's a pretty simple operation from there. The reason you need a Live environment is the hard drive can't be in use while resizing partitions.

I believe there's something called Clonezilla to clone things also but I'm no expert on that, so take with a grain of salt.

Edit: just to add to this for anyone else reading, Linux can get pretty messy when it runs low on space due to optimisation/fragmentation issues, so always err on the 'more is better' side.

Honestly if you still have a dual install of windows, just use the windows partition manager. It's going to be much easier if you're still new to linux and there are going to be tons more guides you can find online. Obviously you'll have to use a partitioner in linux when you wipe your windows installation, but that's a different matter.
